scope: R192: device-side profiling is unsupported on this chip, so the bubble hypothesis cannot be directly confirmed
goal: directly confirm or refute R190's pipeline-bubble inference, which underpins the belief that the FA 1.5x is reachable

tool_found.note: exactly the cube/vector/MTE pipe split that would settle the question

blocker.error: Device profiling is not supported on current chip
blocker.also: msprof fails to start with a missing libascendalog.so and only offers coarser granularity
blocker.conclusion: occupancy timelines are not obtainable with the available tooling on this chip

evidence_strength_for_bubble_hypothesis.evidence: cube 24 percent, vector at most 21 percent, HBM 23 percent, all low at once
Bc=384 fastest, Bc=128 with 2.4x the tiles is 1.65x slower
evidence_strength_for_bubble_hypothesis.strength: fairly strong, consistent with a sizeable fixed per-tile cost

evidence_strength_for_bubble_hypothesis.evidence: Bc=304 is only 8.9 percent slower than 384
evidence_strength_for_bubble_hypothesis.strength: strong, rules out cube fragmentation as the main cause

evidence_strength_for_bubble_hypothesis.evidence: softmax at 12 ops per element would still use only 21 percent of the vector peak
evidence_strength_for_bubble_hypothesis.strength: moderate to strong, rules out vector throughput

honest_statement: the bubble hypothesis has indirect support but no direct observation; it must not be described as confirmed

alternatives_not_needing_a_profiler.idea: fit time = a*tiles + b*flops over the R191 configurations, where a>0 demonstrates a fixed per-tile cost
alternatives_not_needing_a_profiler.status: can be done immediately from existing data

alternatives_not_needing_a_profiler.idea: measure an empty kernel with the same blockDim and wave count to size the per-wave fixed cost

next: fit the R191 five points to separate per-tile fixed cost from per-flop cost - this is direct evidence that needs no profiler
